coverage_claim: WM-ACT-047 covers one source-qualified medical procedure occurrence or explicit non-performance from request and authorization bindings through readiness, performance, immediate outcome, output and safety links, correction, protected use, retention and projection. It separates the event from procedure definitions, requests, plans, schedules, tasks, encounters, consent, participants, devices, observations, reports, conditions, adverse events and records. Specialty profiles, jurisdiction rules, the candidate Care Plan containment edge, implementation testing and independent external review remain deferred.

boundary_decision.rationale: The subject-model entry kind event is sound because the model represents one procedure occurrence, attempt or explicit non-performance with occurrence identity, subject, performers, time, status and consequences. The frozen registry record_plane is world-model and its catalogue entry_kind is standalone-mm; neither is the model-research schema entry_kind axis.

decisions.concept: Procedure definition, request, plan, task and occurrence separation
decisions.rationale: FHIR and openEHR support distinct reusable definitions, requests or instructions, workflow fulfillment and performed action records. The event owns what was attempted or done and binds external intent without absorbing it.

decisions.concept: Performed technique and planned procedure separation
decisions.rationale: Procedure code, method, site, approach, components, devices and deviations record actual performance independently of the request. The event never treats scheduling, readiness or an order as proof of performance.

decisions.concept: Completion, outcome, observation, complication and adverse-event separation
decisions.rationale: Completed status proves only event completion. Immediate outcome, measured observations, reports, complications and adverse events remain distinct source-qualified records, and a relation does not prove causation.

The registry ledger records Care Plan / Episode CONTAINS WM-ACT-047 as candidate metadata. The specification may reference planning context but may not publish this edge as approved or infer cascade behavior.

WHO and Joint Commission sources support subject, site, procedure, consent and team verification, but exact checkpoints, exceptions and authority require specialty, institution and jurisdiction profiles.

Released performance, device-use, status and outcome records are not overwritten. Corrections create successors, and primary performance evidence remains distinguishable from reported history or billing-derived data.

FHIR R5 Procedure and ServiceRequest are Trial Use at maturity level 4, CarePlan and AdverseEvent are Trial Use at maturity level 2, FHIR Observation is normative, and ICHI is a development publication. Every FHIR, openEHR, SNOMED, ICHI, OMOP and UDI alignment must pin version and loss; no universal conformance is claimed.

One Claude Sonnet and one Grok 4.6 attempt for WM-ACT-047 each timed out after 120 seconds. Owner-approved policy permits source-grounded Codex fallback after this separate no-tools audit. Confidence remains medium and assurance remains reviewable-draft with a visible absence-of-external-review hold.

publication_holds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok 4.6 attempt for WM-ACT-047 each timed out after 120 seconds. No external result was admitted; the model remains a reviewable draft after the separate no-tools audit.
Registry edge approval hold: WM-ACT-049 Care Plan / Episode CONTAINS WM-ACT-047 remains candidate metadata. This blocks complete relationship claims, not standalone reviewable-draft publication.

Clinical-specialty hold: surgery, anesthesia, imaging, laboratory, rehabilitation, counseling, obstetric, dental, device, transfusion and other procedure families need specialized method, resource, safety, outcome and follow-up rules.
Jurisdiction and institution hold: consent, qualification, scope of practice, time-out, reporting, retention, correction and disclosure must bind applicable policy before operational use.

Interoperability hold: FHIR resource maturity varies, ICHI is a development publication, and all FHIR, openEHR, SNOMED, ICHI, OMOP and UDI projections require version-pinned mappings, licensing checks where applicable, loss declarations and clinical validation.
deferred_research: Approve or reject the WM-ACT-049 containment edge and define cardinality, plan membership, performed-activity binding and non-cascade semantics.
Create specialty profiles for surgery, anesthesia, imaging, laboratory, rehabilitation, counseling, obstetric, dental, device and transfusion procedures.
Create jurisdiction and institution profiles for consent, performer qualification, safety verification, reporting, correction, retention and access.
Test release-pinned FHIR, openEHR, SNOMED CT, ICHI, OMOP CDM and UDI mappings with mapping-loss and round-trip evidence.
Obtain supplemental Claude or Grok review and resolve any material challenge before canonical promotion.
